transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 mins | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Tom (BeaconHealth Head of AI), Sara (BeaconHealth Security), Ned (BeaconHealth Platform)

Summary: quick POC scoping focused on security/compliance requirements for a pilot. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing for benchmarks, timelines, and specific security asks (SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS). Agreed to run a week-long benchmark and exchange docs.

00:00:05 Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, good to see you. quick intros?
00:00:12 Tom (BeaconHealth): yep tom alvarez, head of ai at beaconhealth, we run clinical triage and patient messaging, looking at ml ops infra for household models.
00:00:20 Sara (BeaconHealth): sara kim, security lead, i'll be looking at compliance, data flows, encryption, etc.
00:00:26 Ned (BeaconHealth): ned park, platform eng, i'll help with the infra side and run the benchmarks.
00:00:30 Jordan (Redwood): great, i'm jordan, AE, and priya is our solutions eng. we usually run a short scoping call to capture success criteria and lock down the security must-haves for a pilot.
00:00:45 Priya (Redwood): hi all, quick note: we'll propose a hosted pilot with VPC peering or private endpoints — or dedicated if you want reserved capacity. today let's focus on your security checklist so we can scope the POC.

00:01:12 Tom: high level — success criteria: parity on response quality vs our current model, throughput to support ~20 qps peak for the demo, latency sub 400ms for 95th p50 we can tolerate higher but 95th should be under 400ms, and of course no PHI leakage and auditability.
00:01:35 Sara: from security: SOC 2 is table stakes, we're also tracking ISO 27001. we need SSO via SAML (Okta), RBAC for team separation, audit logs shipped to our SIEM, and customer-controlled KMS for keys if possible. also data residency: US-only for the pilot.
00:01:58 Priya: got it. we are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO 27001 attestation — we'll share the docs. we support SAML SSO and role-based access; our console has granular roles. audit logs are available via streaming (syslog/HTTPS) and we can arrange log forwarding to your Splunk/Datadog.
00:02:22 Ned: quick clarification: when you say KMS, do you support bringing your own key, or is it only platform-managed?
00:02:29 Priya: we support customer-managed keys via KMS in private deployments and dedicated. For hosted, we offer an optional KMS integration with vendor-managed HSMs with separation controls; we can discuss bringing your KMS in the VPC option.
00:02:45 Tom: ok for the pilot we'd prefer an isolated environment — if we could do dedicated capacity that would reduce noise in the benchmarks. but cost is a factor for a short pilot.
00:02:56 Jordan: typical pattern: start with a short hosted POC with private endpoints + VPC peering to keep data paths private, then if performance/noise becomes an issue we move to dedicated reserved capacity for a longer pilot. that lets you validate functionality quickly.

00:03:18 Sara: about audit logs — we need 12 months of retention and log integrity (immutable), and chain-of-custody for admin actions. can you produce a sample audit event schema?
00:03:30 Priya: yes, we'll share the audit schema. events include request meta (user, token, route), model version, inference inputs hash, response id, and admin changes. small caveat: the transcribed request payload is redacted by default for privacy but we can provide hashed pointers for traceability.
00:03:53 Tom: for success criteria we will define a quality threshold on our eval set (>= 92% accuracy on intent classification and no PII leakage in 3 runs). throughput wise we expect to run a 24-hour benchmark with a synthetic 20 qps peak and 5 qps sustained.
00:04:12 Priya: that matches our benchmark slate. we'll include options: continuous batching on, different quantization profiles, and prefix caching toggles. also will test cold vs warm KV cache (kv cash was typo in my notes earlier, kv cache).

00:04:30 Ned: on dataset — we'll anonymize ~1k records and provide 10k synth queries to emulate production. what's your recommended token budget for the pilot?
00:04:38 Priya: recommend planning for 100M tokens for a week-long run at that scale; depends on prompt length though. we'll produce an estimate once we see the sample prompts.
00:04:47 Jordan: timeline suggestion: exchange security artifacts this week, provision pilot infra next week, run benchmarks the week of 2025-10-13, then run a quick review and decision by 2025-10-20. is that feasible?
00:04:59 Tom: sounds reasonable.

00:05:10 Sara: a few security specifics — SAML metadata must support assertion encryption, we need SCIM provisioning or Okta group sync, and RBAC should let us restrict inference keys to read-only observers vs admin. Also support for session timeout and MFA enforced.
00:05:31 Priya: we support encrypted assertions, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained API keys with scopes. session timeout and MFA enforced via your IdP.

00:05:48 Ned: network topology — for private endpoints will you provide a diagram? we need CIDR ranges for routing and route tables to allow peering.
00:05:56 Priya: yes, we'll send a network diagram and a minimal firewall/NACL checklist. note: for on-prem we also have an appliance model but that's heavier.

00:06:10 Tom: any compliance gotchas? e.g., logs containing PII — how do you handle redaction?
00:06:16 Priya: by default request payloads are redacted in logs; we store hashes and pointers for trace. for customers needing full traceability we can enable encrypted retention with customer-managed KMS, but that triggers additional signing and access controls.

00:06:35 Sara: what about penetration testing and attestations? we will likely need a pen test window and SOC2 evidence.
00:06:40 Jordan: we publish our SOC 2 report to signed NDAs/secure share; we can coordinate a limited pen test in the pilot environment and agree on rules of engagement.

00:07:02 Tom: let's talk benchmarks — priya, how will you measure latency and error modes?
00:07:08 Priya: we'll run an automated harness that records per-request latency, 50/95/99, throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, and model output diffs vs your gold set. we'll test with and without batching, with different batch sizes, and with/without KV cache priming. We'll also run a failure mode test: simulate a model fallback to smaller variant to observe graceful degradation.
00:07:35 Ned: for fallback — do you have policy-based routing so requests can go to a cheaper model automatically?
00:07:40 Priya: yes, smart routing policies can fallback to compatible model variants in the same family; we can show how to configure thresholds for latency and error rates.

00:07:58 Sara: audit log detail: we need admin action records, token issuance, token revocation, and redwood engineer access logs (for private deployments).
00:08:06 Priya: access logs for our team are also recorded and we can include privileged access check-ins and timeboxed access for troubleshooting.

00:08:20 Tom: legal/procurement — we need a short MSA amendment for pilot, with liability caps and data handling clauses. what's typical for you?
00:08:28 Jordan: we have a pilot MSA template that covers scope, data handling, and a two-week limited liability clause for the pilot; we'll share it with your procurement team.

00:08:40 Ned: technical check — will you need us to open firewall egress to any external endpoints for model pulls or is everything inside the VPC?
00:08:48 Priya: model artifacts are pulled internaly during provisioning; for hosted private endpoints nothing should leave your VPC other than the peered path. we'll clarify minimal egress rules in the network doc.

00:09:05 Tom: a question about model versions and rollouts — can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts? we want deterministic results for the benchmarks.
00:09:13 Priya: yes, you can pin versioned artifacts; we'll create a dedicated route with a pinned model and version. Canary/A-B rollouts are supported but for the benchmark we'll pin to a single version to be deterministic.

00:09:36 Sara: encryption in transit and at rest? are TLS 1.2/1.3 supported and at-rest encryption with AES-256?
00:09:44 Priya: yes TLS 1.2/1.3, and at-rest encryption with AES-256; for bring-your-own-kms we support customer key rotation policies.

00:09:56 Jordan: i want to capture the success criteria again: 1) quality threshold on your eval set (>=92%), 2) latency p95 < 400ms under benchmark load, 3) throughput 20 qps peak sustained for burst periods, 4) security controls validated (SOC2/ISO paperwork, SSO, RBAC, audit logs forwarded), and 5) deployment path documented for next steps (dedicated vs hosted).
00:10:22 Tom: yep that's what we'll sign off on.

00:10:30 Priya: i'll outline the benchmark matrix: test cases for cold/warm cache, batching sizes [1, 8, 32], quantization configs (fp16, int8-ish), and model variants. We'll collect latency, throughput, GPU util, and quality diffs.
00:10:45 Ned: will the benchmark harness require us to run a local runner or will it be hosted from your side?
00:10:50 Priya: we can run it from your infra (preferred for network parity) or from our test runner. for best apples-to-apples we'll give a dockerized harness you run in your environment and we orchestrate the model endpoint.

00:11:08 Sara: what about logging identity — will the audit events include Okta user IDs or federated IDs?
00:11:14 Priya: yes, audit events can map to Okta subject claims; we'll include ID mapping in the schema we send.

00:11:25 Tom: any blockers on data residency? we need US-only for now.
00:11:29 Priya: we have region controls; for hosted pilots we'll ensure endpoints live in US-east or US-west per your choice.

00:11:38 Jordan: to summarize action items: we'll share SOC2/ISO docs, network diagram, audit schema, and the benchmark plan. you will provide sample data, IdP metadata, and procurement contacts. We'll schedule the benchmark run for week of 2025-10-13.
00:11:54 Tom: sounds good.

00:12:05 Sara: one last thing — do you have a feature for redaction testing? like we want to validate that PHI is not stored in clear text after inference in logs.
00:12:13 Priya: yes, we can enable redaction enforcement and run tests where we inject synthetic PHI and verify log redaction; we can include that in the benchmark.

00:12:28 Jordan: perfect. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff and attach the docs. thanks everyone.

00:12:36 Tom: thanks all.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (sam-el for SAML, sock two for SOC 2) — faithful to raw transcription style.

End of transcript.
